scope: the hot-path probe at 0x66ECA1 captured ONE bit read and then broke the client - but the single record is informative: the first bit read of a snapshot is at bit 243, not bit 0
what_it_tells_us: the first bit read of a snapshot happens at bit 243, i.e. the header consumes about 30 BYTES before the first bit-level field
that is consistent with the header containing configstrings and commands, which are byte/string data
so the bit stream genuinely starts partway into the body, which is why the earlier assumption 'bits 0..1307 are the header' was only approximately right
why_the_run_failed: 0x66ECA1 is on the hot path - it executes for every single bit read
the probe fired once and the client then died, which is the same failure mode seen with other mid-function hot addresses
so this address cannot be used for repeated sampling

and the hot path cannot be probed to correct them
so the id must be settled by STATIC analysis: read 0x671650 end to end and follow the value from the byte fetches to the store at 0x7859358, with the actual call site of 0x66EC30 in that function
